Phone control lets the local engine launch apps and operate them on a background screen through an authorized Shizuku, wireless debugging or root channel. Screen content may be sent to the model provider for your task. You can stop the task from DSH or its notification. Main-screen accessibility control is currently unavailable. Enable only if you understand and accept this access.
Write actions will run without asking. This may send messages, change settings, or modify files. App rules and sensitive area restrictions still apply.
This reduces confirmation or blocking for this app. Allow phone control under the selected rule?
The local engine and its tools will be able to read and modify shared phone files. Android file access must also be granted. Continue?
Restore the built in deny and confirmation rules? Your custom app rules will be replaced.
Local engine restart requested to apply phone access.
Enter a valid Android package name.
Stop the current phone task before removing a sensitive area restriction.
Phone file access was not granted. The engine setting remains unchanged.
Enter the six digit pairing code.
Enter a port between 1 and 65535, or leave it blank.
The selected phone channel changed. Try again with the current selection.
Could not read phone settings. Refresh to try again.
The phone setting could not be changed. Its actual state is shown after refresh.
Root gives the phone control process elevated access to this device. Continue only if you trust your local tasks. Your root manager will ask you to authorize dsh-compose.
Keep your finger on the button for about 1.5 seconds. Releasing early cancels.

AI may change permissions, accessibility and developer options; install, update or uninstall apps; and interact with security settings and notification buttons. A mistake could revoke access, weaken protection or damage device settings.

AI may type passwords, verification codes and payment codes, and use codes seen in messages or notifications to sign in. A mistake may expose an account or authorize a payment. Typed secret values stay masked in the action log.
AI may read conversations and settings inside dsh-compose, tap its controls, and change its settings. It could change its own access or disrupt your tasks.

Once enabled, AI can perform these operations without your confirmation where the selected policy allows. Content in pages, messages or files may mislead it. You bear any resulting loss to accounts, money, data or the device; dsh-compose and its developers accept no liability. Enable only temporarily when needed, turn it off afterwards, and avoid enabling it on devices holding payment or banking information.
Phone actions were stopped, but one or more local conversations could not be cancelled. Check running conversations and stop them there.
Works on a hidden screen while you use your phone
This phone needs Android 14 or later to use this feature.
Sui module on Magisk or KernelSU
No extra app, uses wireless debugging
Install Shizuku first (free and open source). If you use tools like Ice Box or Brevent, you may already have it.
Open Shizuku and follow “Start via Wireless debugging” (requires Wi-Fi). This page refreshes when you return.
Turn on Developer options: tap “Build number” 7 times in “About phone”. On Xiaomi, tap “OS version” in “My device → Detailed info and specs”; on vivo, tap “Software version”.
Turn on “Wireless debugging” in Developer options while connected to Wi-Fi. Developer options is usually in “System” or “Additional settings”.
Return here and tap “Start pairing”. DSH sends a notification.
In “Wireless debugging”, tap “Pair device with pairing code” to see a 6-digit code.
Pull down notifications and enter the code in DSH’s notification, or fill it in below. Once paired, tap “Connect”.
The number after the colon in “IP address & port” below the pairing code
Keep the screen on and unlocked.
With Shizuku or Direct ADB, stay on Wi-Fi with Wireless debugging on.
Let AI do what’s yours by default
Fill in passwords, verification and payment codes
Tap and type inside DSH Compose
Can’t turn on while a task is running
Once on, the consequences are yours. Turn on only when needed, and off when done.
See confirmations and task results in time

When a step needs your decision, a DSH Compose card appears. If the card is unavailable, the app tries a notification or returns here. Allow phone-control notifications and pop-up alerts in system settings.
Allow pop-up alerts for phone-control notifications

In the system permissions for DSH Compose, check “Display pop-up windows while running in the background”, if available. Allowing it can help the app return automatically. Menu names vary by system version.
If the app does not return when a task finishes, tap “Task complete · View result”. If system notifications or background windows are blocked, you may need to open DSH Compose yourself.
Run a phone task to see its actions here. Task progress appears in Live Notification.
No actions in the last hour. Select all time to see earlier records.
